Hi Darren — following up with a technical breakdown. I kept this at an operational level so it maps to what you'll see in evidence exports.

Summary (short):
- Live storage: deletion is applied immediately to primary data stores (seconds to minutes after the request completes).
- Short-term snapshots (hot snapshots, TTL 0-7 days): tombstone + incremental compaction means data becomes logically inaccessible within minutes; physical reclaim occurs on next GC sweep (typically within 24 hours).
- Long-term snapshots / archives (default retention 90 days): these are immutable at snapshot time and retained until their TTL expires or a targeted purge job runs. Typical retention windows are 30/90/365 days depending on policy.
- Cross-region replication: asynchronous replication to DR regions is designed for RPO < 4 hours. In practice, worst-case replication lag is ~4 hours; a deletion on primary won't remove already-replicated snapshot files until the snapshot lifecycle/purge phase runs in the target region.

Detailed behavior and evidence you can expect:
1) Tombstone and logical deletion: we record a deletion event (deletion_id, timestamp, initiating_account) in the audit log and update the object index. You will see the event almost immediately in the audit log export (we can slice by deletion_id).
2) Snapshot manifests: snapshots include manifests with object digests; when a purge runs we update the manifest and produce a "purge manifest" for that snapshot run. We can export the manifest diff for a given snapshot id as evidence.
3) Offsite/immutable archives: by design these are write-once for retention TTL. For EU-scoped PII we support targeted purge jobs where we identify affected chunks (by digest map) and rewrite the archive without the chunks; turnaround depends on archive size and legal scope. Typical timeline: 3-14 days for targeted archive rewrite.
4) Legal hold interaction: items under legal hold are exempt from automated purge. We annotate hold_id in manifests and audit logs. Releasing a hold triggers the normal purge pipeline (not instantaneous).

Expedited purge options (compliance exception):
- Manual expedited archive rewrite (APO): we can schedule a prioritized job. SLA target: 72 hours for small datasets (<50GB), 3-14 days for larger sets. Requires PO + support-level authorization.
- Certification package: we can provide a SOC2-style evidence bundle (audit log slice, snapshot manifests, purge-manifests). Generating a complete bundle usually takes 1-3 business days depending on the date range.

Notes on EU residency: if you have a strict EU-only requirement we recommend enabling our EU-only replication policy (blocks cross-region replication for selected datasets). If cross-region DR is required, we can map and tag EU-only PII to ensure targeted purge paths exist.
